run_metadata.coverage_summary: All source tiers were attempted (Tier 1 Commonwealth + all states/territories; Tier 2 councils/GBEs/universities/health; Tier 3 private-sector e-sourcing hubs and major-buyer portals; plus a source-discovery sweep). Connectivity was re-tested at the start of the run: WebFetch returned EGRESS_BLOCKED for every host, including a neutral control fetch to en.wikipedia.org, confirming a session-wide organisation egress block rather than a portal login wall (same condition as the 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-01 runs — now three consecutive days). Proxy status (/root/.ccr/__agentproxy/status) shows enabled=true, bundleCoversEveryHost=true and recentRelayFailures=[], consistent with a deny-by-default allowlist that permits only infrastructure hosts and no external tender domains. WebSearch still works (it routes through the Anthropic API, not the egress proxy) and surfaced candidate opportunities and source leads. Because the spec's fidelity rule requires every tender detail to come from the actual notice or its documents, and no notice page could be opened, no opportunity could be verified — so this run records ZERO tenders. The source-discovery sweep did surface two buyer-originated council procurement pages not present in any prior run (Noosa Shire Council and Toowoomba Regional Council, both on VendorPanel); these are recorded in discovered_sources at medium confidence with a clear note that they were surfaced via WebSearch and could NOT be fetch-verified this run due to the egress block. No tenders, deliverables, dates, contacts, or corporate opportunities were invented.
gaps: CRITICAL BLOCKER (recurring, 3rd consecutive run): Outbound HTTPS page fetching is blocked for this session. WebFetch returns {"error_type":"EGRESS_BLOCKED"} for all hosts and a direct control fetch to https://en.wikipedia.org also failed, proving a session-wide (organisation egress allowlist) block, not a portal-specific wall. Proxy status shows enabled=true, bundleCoversEveryHost=true, recentRelayFailures=[], consistent with a deny-by-default allowlist that permits only infrastructure hosts (Anthropic API, npm, pypi, crates, go, gcloud/gh) and no external tender domains. Per the proxy README a 403/EGRESS_BLOCKED must be reported, not retried or routed around.
Tier 1 Commonwealth — AusTender (https://www.tenders.gov.au, /atm) EGRESS_BLOCKED; no ATM verifiable this run.

Tier 1 states/territories — tenders.nsw.gov.au / buy.nsw.gov.au, tenders.vic.gov.au / buyingfor.vic.gov.au, etender.hpw.qld.gov.au (formerly qtenders) / supply.qld.gov.au, tenders.wa.gov.au, tenders.sa.gov.au, tenders.tas.gov.au, tendersonline.nt.gov.au (QTOL), tenders.act.gov.au — all EGRESS_BLOCKED. No portal URL changes could be verified because none could be opened.

Tier 2 (councils/GBEs/universities/health) — VendorPanel public tenders, individual council sites, Sydney Water / Melbourne Water / SA Water / Water Corporation WA / Power and Water NT, CSIRO procurement, university and Local Health District tender pages — all EGRESS_BLOCKED. Water-corporation supplier portals (WA eProcurement, SA Water Supplier Portal, Melbourne Water via Buying for Victoria, Power & Water via NT QTOL) were re-confirmed by WebSearch as still-active channels but could not be opened to read live opportunities.

Tier 3 (private sector/construction) — service.ariba.com (SAP Ariba Discovery), BHP/Rio Tinto/Fortescue/Woodside/Santos supplier portals, Woolworths Partner Hub, Coles/Wesfarmers supplier pages, Qantas (Coupa), CBA/Westpac/NAB/ANZ, Telstra/Optus/TPG, AGL/Origin, EstimateOne, ICN Gateway — all EGRESS_BLOCKED. Invitation-only consultancy RFPs remain out of scope by definition; registration/login-gated corporate RFx could not be recorded because even the public portal landing pages were unreachable. No corporate tenders were invented.

LANDSCAPE NOTE (WebSearch-only, re-confirmed this run): Queensland is running a phased replacement of QTenders by VendorPanel Marketplace (supply.qld.gov.au) as its single procurement solution; the two systems run in parallel during transition, with ~90 state agencies and ~70 QLD councils already onboarded. Suppliers must keep a QTenders registration until QTenders fully integrates with VendorPanel. Confirm the live state per buyer on the notice page once egress is restored.

LANDSCAPE NOTE (WebSearch-only, carry-over): search snippets continue to indicate an SAP Ariba Business Network -> Coupa migration wave affecting some Australian buyers, with Ariba being phased down through March 2026. Confirm the current e-sourcing platform for affected buyers (which portal to register on) once egress is restored before relying on it.

UNVERIFIED CANDIDATE OPPORTUNITIES (surfaced by WebSearch only; NOT fetched, NOT recorded as tenders; likely stale/closed and must be confirmed on the notice page before use): a DFAT RFT snippet showed a 1 Oct 2026 close date and a 'Western Province Partnership Mid-Term Review' RFT showed a 28 Sep 2026 close (appears CLOSED). Prior-run carry-over leads (Tasmania aged-care greenfield EOI; Melbourne Water Field Services Panel RFT; Australia Post OTC Services EOI; various NT QTOL and Brisbane City Council items) could not be re-verified this run. Treat all as leads, not confirmed opportunities.

RECOMMENDATION TO RESTORE COVERAGE: add the tender-portal domains to this environment's egress allowlist (or run the routine where WebFetch is permitted). Until then daily runs can only produce empty-but-honest tender results because no notice can be verified; only WebSearch-level source discovery is possible.
